content:
Instagram now offers an iPhone-exclusive new feature that can automatically create Reels. You just pick video clips and with one tap you can generate an edited version.

However, Meta is being very cautious and doesn't want creators to feel that this feature can replace their manual editing skills...

Their caution even extends to the feature's name — it's called First Draft, meaning it only provides a starting point for creation.

The company shared the process and example results via a post on Threads.

Users can also create a first draft edit immediately after filming.

There are two ways to use this feature: 1. Open the Reels media library → select 1 or more clips → tap the "First draft" button at the bottom of the screen → review the edit → go to the full editor or publish. 2. Open the camera within Instagram → film content → tap the "First draft" button → review the edit → go to the full editor to publish

Some creators questioned why this feature was placed in the main Instagram app rather than the Edits app. The company responded that it can be offered in both apps if needed. Currently this feature is only available on iPhone, with the Android version expected to launch later.
